value.first: He's right at the age to start. I'd go with iron-first solids with early-and-often allergens: iron foods first because his stored iron runs low around 6 months, and allergens early because waiting doesn't protect. Early peanut cut peanut allergy about 80% in a big trial. Days 1-7: once he sits up in the high chair unsupported, offer a spoon or two of iron cereal, puréed beef or mashed lentils, building to twice a day. Milk continues as usual.
value.second: Week 2, peanut: one morning, thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter with warm water or purée, give a tiny taste, wait 10 minutes, then the rest. Watch him two hours, nothing else new that day. Next day or two: hard-scrambled egg, same routine. Then one new allergen a day: yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, fish. Once tolerated, keep each about twice a week. Gagging is normal and noisy. No honey before 12 months.
value.third: If you'd rather skip purées, baby-led weaning with soft finger foods works with the same allergen schedule. It's working when he opens up for the spoon and gagging fades. Have lumpy and soft finger foods going by 9 months. If he has moderate-to-severe eczema, or any food brings hives or vomiting, stop that food and see your provider before the next one.
